body: Silicon sampling generates survey respondents by having a large language model (LLM) answer a survey as a person with given demographic attributes, and the resulting synthetic populations are increasingly used in place of human ones. Existing evaluations focus on individual-answer accuracy, per-question answer distributions, and correlations across questions. None of these compares the respondents themselves, so a generator whose respondents have combinations of answers found in no human respondent can still score well if it reproduces every answer distribution. We propose the respondent coverage gap (RCG), which represents each respondent as a point defined by their complete answer profile and measures how far each human respondent is from the nearest generated one, relative to the distance between human samples. On two US social surveys, all six LLMs we evaluate leave human respondents uncovered, and under our main settings, they fall behind a baseline that samples each answer independently from the human marginals. Across the prompting and inference settings we test, every LLM has a higher RCG than a Gaussian copula fitted to the human data.
summaryZh: 硅样本匹配答案，但不匹配受访者。硅样本通过大型语言模型 (LLM) 以具有给定人口统计属性的人的身份回答调查，生成调查受访者，并且越来越多地使用由此产生的合成群体来代替人类群体。现有的评估侧重于个人答案的准确性、每个问题的答案分布以及问题之间的相关性。
